subject: botany
question_text: Define with examples endospermic and non-endospermic seeds.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack botany section (book p.17, VSAQ 4). Botany holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no botany board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question
Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants · 2 marks

steps.label: Endospermic seeds
lines: Endospermic seeds: the endosperm persists in
the mature seed and stores the food.
steps.why: The whole classification rests on one question — is the endosperm still there in the mature seed? Here it persists, so the seed keeps its food in the endosperm. These are also called albuminous seeds.
common_mistakes: Giving groundnut or bean as the example — those are the non-endospermic pair.
Defining by cotyledon number. Monocot/dicot is a different classification.
steps.memory_tip: Coconut water and the white kernel ARE endosperm you can see — coconut is the endospermic anchor.
steps.margin_note: Definition plus one correct example earns the mark; two examples are safer.

steps.label: Non-endospermic seeds
lines: Non-endospermic seeds: the endosperm is fully
used up by the developing embryo by the time
steps.why: The contrast completes the definition: the same endosperm forms in both, but here the embryo consumes it during development, so the mature seed has none — the food sits in the cotyledons instead.
common_mistakes: Writing 'endosperm never forms'. It forms in both; here it is consumed.
Swapping the example pairs between the two types.
steps.memory_tip: A groundnut splits into two fat cotyledons and nothing else — the food moved into them because the endosperm was used up.
steps.margin_note: The boxed contrast line is the one-glance summary the examiner rewards.

insider_note: Both marks turn on the phrase 'by the time the ovule becomes a seed' — the endosperm forms in every angiosperm seed; persist or get used up is the only difference.
